items.title: HomeKit Weekly: Meross’s new presence sensor splits a room into three zones for Apple Home
items.summary:
Presence sensors tell Apple Home when someone is in a particular room, which is awesome for running automations based on that. They don’t tell it where in the room you are, though. That’s why these types of automations end up being all-or-nothing type things: you walk into a room, and every light comes on at full brightness, whether you came in to read at your desk or to grab something off the counter. The Meross MS605 splits its detection range into three distance zones, and each of them shows up in Apple Home as its own presence sensor so you can build automations around them.

more…

YouTube is not done tinkering with its mobile app, and the streaming giant’s latest redesign is making the platform’s Home feed a lot more chaotic.

items.title: Samsung is holding back these 30+ Galaxy AI features for the Galaxy S27
items.summary:
Credit: Pankil Shah / Android Authority 

TL;DR 

Code in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 ties a long list of new Galaxy AI features to “Galaxy AI version 20271,” which Samsung’s own code labels as the S27’s AI version. 
 Gated Galaxy S27 features span Gallery’s Recompose, new Camera ProScan and Log LUT tools, full-table AI select, expanded Scam Detection languages, and an Audio eraser for your calls. 
 Several 20271 features, including Gen Video credits, Samsung Browser’s Ask anything, and Now Brief’s Bixby action card, appear tied to a paid Galaxy AI Premium tier.

Over the past week, we’ve found dozens of new Galaxy AI features in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 for the Galaxy S26 Ultra , but many refuse to run on the device. When we dug into Samsung’s Scam Detection features for third-party calling apps , we noticed they check for something called “ Galaxy AI version 20271 ,” a level our S26 Ultra doesn’t meet. Now, we’ve found code that spells out what that number means: It’s the Galaxy S27’s AI version. items.title: PSA: Amazon’s 2026 Kindle back panels are popping off when owners remove their cases
items.summary:
TL;DR 

The removable back panels on the 2026 Kindle and Kindle Paperwhite can accidentally detach when removing a protective case. 
 The issue occurs even with Amazon’s official cover, but hasn’t been observed on the aluminum Kindle or Paperwhite Signature Edition. 
 Amazon says owners can simply press the panel back into place, although reassembly can cause alignment issues. 

We got our first hint that Amazon was preparing to make Kindle batteries easier to replace back in May, and the company delivered on that front with the launch of its redesigned Kindle lineup in October. It’s a welcome change for devices that people often keep for years, but some owners of the 2026 Kindle and Kindle Paperwhite are discovering that the removable back panel can come loose long before it’s time for a new battery.

A Kindle owner on Reddit demonstrated how their Ube Kindle comes apart when removing a protective case. TikTok creator Jackie’s Book Tally shared a similar experience, showing how trying to peel away a clear case to put some stickers on the back of her Kindle causes the device’s housing to separate.
items.t: PSA: Amazon’s 2026 Kindle back panels are popping off when owners remove their cases

items.title: iOS and HarmonyOS gain ground as Android's Q3 share hits a record low
items.summary:
Last month Counterpoint Research (CR) told us that the Q3 smartphone market dropped 20%, and today the firm has published its breakdown of sales share by operating system for the same quarter. Unsurprisingly, the memory crisis has left its mark here too.

According to CR, global smartphone sales were down 16% year-over-year in Q3, as the RAM supply crisis hit the entry segment hard and pushed prices up in the higher tiers. items.title: X finally launches parental controls for teen accounts
items.summary:
X says it's not designed for or promoted to children, but anyone aged 13 or older can sign up, and teen accounts already default to protected mode, with sensitive media restricted and targeted ads blocked. Today the platform is adding its first-ever Parental Controls on top of those defaults, aimed at families with teens aged 13 to 17.

With Parental Controls, a parent or guardian can see how much time their teen has spent on X over the past week and set a daily limit. They can also require approval for new followers (which makes the account private as well), limit For You recommendations...
items.t: X finally launches parental controls for teen accounts

items.title: The US will hit China and 13 other trading partners with fresh tariffs, affecting Apple
items.summary:
The Trump administration has proposed new tariffs on imports from 14 US trading partners, including China, India, South Korea, Japan, and the European Union. The planned tariffs are under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, which is a different legal mechanism from the one Trump previously used, and which was subsequently struck down by the Supreme Court in February.

Trump's administration uses Section 301 of the 1974 Trade Act to argue that the excessive foreign manufacturing capacity, which leads to cheap imports, hurts the US economy.

Most countries won't have the new tariffs...
items.t: The US will hit China and 13 other trading partners with fresh tariffs, affecting Apple
